title: SQLite backup and restore procedure
description:
Documented and scripted backup/restore path for all SQLite databases to S3 (or local filesystem), so operators can recover from data loss without losing article index state.

Why this issue exists:
SQLite databases hold the article number index, overview index, message-ID map, and group log. Loss of these databases means loss of the article index (articles are still in Kubo/S3 but cannot be found). Operators need a clear, tested backup and restore procedure.

Scope:
- Add POST /admin/backup to the admin endpoint: triggers an online SQLite backup (using the SQLite backup API, safe while the database is live) to a configured destination directory
- Backup filenames include a timestamp: core-20260423T030000Z.db, transit-20260423T030000Z.db, etc.
- Optional: if [backup] s3_bucket is configured, upload the backup files to S3 after writing locally
- Add a --restore flag to each daemon binary: usenet-ipfs-transit --restore core.db transit.db — restores from backup files before starting normally
- Document the full backup/restore procedure in docs/ops/backup_restore.md
- Schedule-based automatic backup: [backup] schedule = '0 2 * * *' (cron syntax, same as GC)

Acceptance criteria:
- POST /admin/backup creates valid SQLite files that can be opened by sqlite3
- A daemon started with --restore from a backup file serves articles that were indexed before the backup
- S3 upload completes and the file is readable from S3
- docs/ops/backup_restore.md covers both the happy path and the 'Kubo is fine but SQLite is lost' disaster scenario
